title: Workload Suite Request Mix (v1) — weights + parameters
body:
Sheet purpose
- Defines v1 request-mix profiles used by the perf suite harness.
- Each profile is a weighted combination of workloads + default parameter distributions.
- Used for: (a) baseline sweeps (Q1 2026), (b) nightly perf-canary, (c) release gating subsets.

Important notes / measurement boundaries
- Token lengths are measured on the *server tokenizer* (same as runtime uses); bins are in tokens.
- TTFT/TPOT metrics follow ADR-0172: TTFT = first token on wire (server boundary), TPOT = inter-token pacing on server stream (exclude client read stalls).
- For mixes with streaming workloads, the harness enforces client read rate >= server send rate to avoid client bottleneck (see Slack eng-runtime/1763935150).
- Cache coverage: report both cold and warm runs where applicable (see Slack eng-runtime/1764196509). In this sheet, cache_mode encodes the intended scenario.

Workload IDs (canonical)
- chat_streaming_short: chat/completions, streaming, short prompts, variable decode.
- chat_streaming_standard: chat/completions, streaming, mid prompts, mid decode.
- tool_calling_bursty: multi-turn with function/tool calls; bursty arrivals.
- long_context_summarization: large prefill, modest decode, non-streaming (or streaming off by default).
- embeddings_high_qps: embeddings endpoint, high-QPS small payloads.

Mix profile rows (normalized table)
- weight_pct must sum to 100 per mix_id.
- concurrency_target is concurrent in-flight requests (or streaming connections) at steady state.
- target_qps is only used for non-streaming modes where the harness drives an arrival rate; streaming tests are primarily concurrency-driven.

Columns
mix_id, mix_name, workload_id, weight_pct, streaming, cache_mode, prompt_len_dist, output_len_dist, tool_calls_dist, concurrency_target, target_qps, ramp_seconds, steady_seconds, notes

TABLE (CSV)

How to use (harness conventions)
- The harness takes mix_id and expands to concrete per-request parameters by sampling the provided distributions.
- Default run segments:
  - warmup: 120s (not in table); excluded from metrics export.
  - ramp: ramp_seconds
  - steady: steady_seconds
- Unless stated otherwise, the harness sets max_inflight = 2 * concurrency_target to allow bursts without immediate client-side throttling.
- cache_mode:
  - cold: no prefix/KV reuse between requests.
  - warm_prefix: fixed prefix pool of size 64; 70% of requests draw from the pool to create repeatable cache hits; remaining 30% are random prefixes.

Why these weights (quick rationale)
- M1 (prod_like_v1) approximates top-line production traffic: chat dominates; embeddings non-trivial; long-context present enough to catch TTFT cliffs.
- M2 (chat_heavy_v1) is the fast iteration mix (lower cost, higher signal on streaming TPOT/TTFT changes).
- M3 (prefill_stress_v1) is the regression “magnifying glass” for prefill/kernels/backpressure.
- M4 (embeddings_throughput_v1) isolates throughput and tail behavior for embeddings.
- M5 (tool_bursty_v1) focuses on queueing fairness + overload behavior under bursty multi-turn tool usage.

Open questions / TODO (v1.1 candidates)
- Confirm whether tool_calling_bursty should be measured as streaming or hybrid (tool call boundaries create micro-non-streaming segments). Current choice: streaming yes; measure TTFT on first assistant token.
- Validate prompt length bins for EU-West separately (telemetry suggests slightly higher mid-bin frequency for some tenants).
- Decide whether to split embeddings into two cohorts: micro (<=32) and small (33-256) with separate SLO-style panels.
- Add an explicit "kv_cache_pressure" workload variant (same as long_context_summarization but higher concurrency + overlapping prefill).

Change log
- 2025-12-18 (RK): initial draft based on telemetry cohort summary (see Confluence ADR-0173).
- 2026-01-07 (CD): aligned bins with methodology draft; added cache_mode column.
- 2026-01-15 (JW): added M5 tool_bursty_v1 and clarified burst model.
- 2026-01-29 (SG/AB): adjusted concurrency defaults for SRE fleet stability (lowered M3 concurrency from 48->36; added longer ramp for M3).
